title: August 2026 producer prices rose at the final-demand and upstream energy surfaces
source_unit: Bureau of Labor Statistics Producer Price Indexes for domestic producers
geography: United States; national producer price indexes for final and intermediate demand

denominator.unit: BLS producer-price index sample and weighting system; release does not disclose a single respondent or transaction-count denominator

observations.method: BLS PPI release comparing seasonally adjusted producer price indexes with the prior month and unadjusted indexes over 12 months.
observations.uncertainty: PPI measures seller-side price change and includes revisions, sample design, weighting, quality adjustment, and category coverage boundaries. It is not a direct measure of retailer margins, consumer prices, firm profitability, or household burden.
observations.subgroup: Final-demand goods, services, and aggregate final-demand categories; no household or individual-firm subgroup estimate.
observations.counterinterpretation: Producer-price movement may be absorbed by margins, passed through with delay, offset by productivity or contracts, or concentrated in firms and products not purchased by a particular household. It does not establish incidence or bargaining power.

observations.period: August 2026 final-demand energy and diesel movement

denominator.unit: BLS final-demand and product-group producer price indexes; release does not disclose a single transaction-count denominator

diesel_fuel.unit: percent monthly increase in the detailed final-demand goods index

final_demand_goods_energy_contribution.value: over three-fourths of the broad-based goods rise

observations.method: BLS product-detail and contribution statements for final-demand goods and energy components.
observations.uncertainty: The product detail is an index movement and contribution decomposition, not a measure of a particular firm's cost, a contract pass-through, or a household's fuel bill. April–July values were revised for late reports and corrections.
observations.subgroup: Final-demand goods and selected fuel/product categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: A sharp diesel index movement can affect transport, agriculture, logistics, and prices differently depending on contracts, inventories, fuel intensity, route, and market power; downstream timing and incidence remain open.

denominator.unit: BLS processed and unprocessed intermediate-demand indexes; release does not disclose a single transaction-count denominator

observations.method: BLS intermediate-demand stage-of-processing indexes, with separate processed and unprocessed goods measures.
observations.uncertainty: Intermediate-demand indexes describe upstream price stages and cannot be added mechanically to CPI or final-demand rates. Revision, stage coverage, quality, timing, and pass-through assumptions remain material.
observations.subgroup: Processed and unprocessed goods for intermediate demand.
observations.counterinterpretation: Upstream inflation can coexist with stable downstream prices if margins, substitution, inventories, contracts, or productivity absorb it; conversely, delayed pass-through can produce later consumer or firm effects.

related_sources.claim: BLS PPI definitions, databases, and methodological context.
August 2026 CPI provides the downstream consumer-price comparison.
BEA income, PCE, and outlays provide aggregate demand and saving context.

boundary: This record adds an official August 2026 producer-price checkpoint to the household, firm, and infrastructure atlas. It does not establish consumer pass-through, firm margins, profits, household costs, bargaining power, policy causality, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequences. The extracted retrieval hash is for the committed release-fact summary; the official release URL remains authoritative.
